title: Telescopic cascode gain stage with PMOS cascode current-source load
description: Design a single-ended telescopic cascode gain stage -- an NMOS common-source input device with an NMOS cascode stacked directly on it, loaded by a PMOS cascode current source -- whose small-signal voltage gain at 1 kHz is at least 85 dB across the full sky130-style tt/ss/ff process corner, 1.62-1.98 V supply, and -40..125 C temperature matrix, while the output node self-biases into the 0.3-0.9 V window and the whole stage (gain branch plus every bias branch) draws no more than 120 uA from the supply. The gain target is what makes the cascode load-bearing rather than decorative: the same stage with both cascode devices removed measures roughly 48 dB on this device set, so no plain common-source stage can reach the gate, however it is sized, without blowing the current budget.

block_spec.spec_class: single-ended high-gain voltage amplifier / cascode gain stage

target_specs.corners: sky130-style tt/ss/ff process x 1.62-1.98V supply x -40..125C

reference.notes: One netlist body, two testbenches over it: an AC gain sweep and a DC-operating-point readout (a deliberately no-op `dc` sweep of the AC-coupled stimulus source, since ngspice implements no `.MEASURE OP`). Real sky130 devices (sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 / sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8) via $PDK_ROOT, per docs/cli/sim.md -- issue #1736 replaced the earlier generic (non-PDK) LEVEL=1 stand-in, whose lack of short-channel output-conductance degradation put its absolute gain (~94-103 dB) well above what a real sky130 telescopic cascode reaches. The real-device reference measures ~86-90 dB across the corner matrix (see casc_amp.spice's header for the sizing this took); what the gate discriminates is still the cascoded-vs-uncascoded contrast, now at a sky130-accurate figure.

source.citation: The cascode gain stage is a standard analog IC design course topic; framed here in the style of AnalogCoder's (Lai et al., AAAI 2025, arXiv 2405.14918) medium-tier task set, not reproduced from that repo (unlicensed).
